Find, **in ascending order and rounded to one decimal place**, the two solutions to the equation $5\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\sqrt{2}=3\operatorname{sec}⁡x-2\sqrt{2}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$

**In ascending order,** the solutions are $x=$
{{field-1}}
and $x=$ 
{{field-2}}.
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{sec}⁡x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{sec}⁡x+\sqrt{2} & =3\operatorname{sec}⁡x-2\sqrt{2} \\ 5\operatorname{sec}⁡x-3\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =-2\sqrt{2}-\sqrt{2} \\ 2\operatorname{sec}⁡x & =-3\sqrt{2} \\ \operatorname{sec}⁡x & =-\frac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{sec}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{cos}⁡x}.$ Therefore the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{cos}⁡x=-\frac{2}{3\sqrt{2}}=-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3}.
$$

Then, we find the principal value of $x,$ rounded to three decimal places:

$$
{x}_{1}=arccos\,(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{3})≈2.062
$$

Our first solution lies in the $2$nd quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}≈\pi -2.062≈1.080.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x<0,$ the second solution must lie in the $3$rd quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}≈1.080.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13977622/assets/c8020c19d17f3e79b825cb4e0cad4471e68ec0e2618a12578115a0fc8c014599.png)

Since the second solution ${x}_{2}$ lies in the $3$rd quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{2} & =\pi +{\theta }_{R} \\  & ≈\pi +1.080 \\  & ≈4.222\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, in ascending order and rounded to one decimal place, the solutions are $x=2.1$ and $x=4.2.$
